data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the subject's failure would make the test itself fail, and the test can only describe the subject when the subject's mutation is not caught by any guard; the 3-of-26 result is a consequence of the fact that the mutations were proposed by models that had read the acceptance record, so the test's constraining force is an artifact of the author's expectations rather than an independent property of the test.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutations were generated independently of the acceptance record, the test's constraining force could be measured.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the sample size were larger than 26, the distribution might be more stable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guard were applied uniformly to all modules, the distribution might differ.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The test's constraining force is relative to the mutations it faces. When the mutations are not independent of the test's author, the test cannot be said to constrain the subject in general; it only describes the subject for the mutations that were proposed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
